...RESPONDENT (BY SRI N. KUMAR, ADVOCATE)
 THIS MFA IS FILED U/S.173(1) OF M.V. ACT, PRAYING TO ALLOW THE APPEAL AND MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 26.12.2019 PASSED IN MVC NO.363/2019 ON THE FILE OF THE COURT OF SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE & MACT AT MALAVALLI, BY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION IN ITS ENTIRETY WITH 18% INTEREST IN THE ENDS OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.

THESE APPEALS COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THROUGH PHYSICAL HEARING/VIDEO CONFERENCING THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 26.12.2019 passed in MVC No.363/2019 by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT at Malavalli, (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioners therein have preferred MFA.No.1513/2021 and respondent - Insurance Company has preferred MFA.No.1504/2021.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that on 07.12.2018 at about 7.30 p.m. the deceased J. Nagaraju, was riding his motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-03-EB-5611 on Maddur main road and when he was near the house of one Police Madaiah in Bhugathagalli village, at that time, KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-10-F-0334 being driven in a rash and negligent manner came and dashed against the motor cycle of the deceased, because of which, the said J. Nagaraju died.
The petitioners are the dependents of the said J. Nagaraju.
They preferred MVC.NO.363/2019.

4. The Tribunal based upon the pleadings and the evidence let in came to the conclusion that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of KSRTC bus and awarded a sum of Rs.10,88,000/- along with interest @ 9% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
5. Aggrieved by the same, respondent - KSRTC has preferred MFA.No.1504/2021 and the petitioners have preferred MFA.No.1513/2021.
6. Admittedly, the accident is of the year 2018.

Though the petitioners have contended that the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month, they have not produced any evidence to Sri Javanegowda vs The Managing Director on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127706629/
3 prove the same before the Tribunal.

sentences.text: Hence, the income of the deceased has to be determined notionally at Rs.12,500/- per month as per the chart prepared by the Lok- Adalath, for the year 2018.
The deceased was aged about 26 years at the time of the accident.
As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in [2009(6) SCC 121], a multiplier of '17' has to be adopted.

entities.text: Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in [2009(6) SCC 121]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the law down by the Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680, 40% needs to be added to his income towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also seen that the petitioner was bachelor at the time of the accident and hence, 50% is deducted towards his personal expenses.
Thus, on the count of loss of dependency, petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.17,85,000/- (12,500 + 40% x 12 x 17 x1/2).

7. Further, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in New India Assurance Co.Ltd.
v. Somwati [(2020)9 SCC 644], there are four dependants and they are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium(Rs.40,000x4= 1,60,000).

entities.text:
New India Assurance Co.Ltd.
v. Somwati [(2020)9 SCC 644]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, petitioners are also entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.
Thus, in all, they are entitled to a sum of Rs.19,75,000/- as against Rs.10,88,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
It is seen that the Tribunal has granted 9% interest on the compensation awarded by it.
In my opinion, it is on the higher side.
Given the bank rate of interest, I am of the opinion that it would be appropriate to reduce the rate of interest at the rate of 6% on the entire compensation amount.

8. Hence, the following:-
ORDER i) Both the appeals are allowed-in-part.

ii) The total compensation awarded by the  Tribunal is modified and enhanced to  Rs.19,75,000/- as against Rs.10,88,000/-
 awarded by the Tribunal.
 iii) The petitioners are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.19,75,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition before the Tribunal till the date of realization and respondent - KSRTC shall pay the said amount within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order;
iv) Amount-in-deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
 v) Draw modified award accordingly;
